fundamentals.margin_analysis: Observed quarterly gross margin (provider statements): 72.4% (FQ ended 2025-07-31), 73.4%, 75.0%, 74.9%, 75.0% (FQ ended 2026-07-31); operating margin rose from 60.8% to 66.2% and net margin was 62.0% in the latest provider quarter. The Q3 FY27 press release (8-K exhibit, SEC, quarter ended 2026-10-25) reports GAAP gross margin 74.8% and non-GAAP 74.9%. However, the Q4 FY27 outlook guides GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin to 71.0%-72.0%, a roughly 3-point step down. Inference: margins are at a high plateau and management guidance signals compression next quarter.

Provider total debt rose from $12.35B (FQ ended 2026-04-30) to $38.35B (FQ ended 2026-07-31) while total equity rose to $228.98B; inference: debt/equity about 0.17. Per the Q3 FY27 8-K balance sheet, long-term debt was about $32.4B, with cash and equivalents $29.1B, marketable debt securities $24.4B and marketable equity securities $44.2B (a total-debt figure is not explicitly stated in the release). fundamentals.growth_outlook: The pipeline's tool-calculated YoY growth is unavailable (gap: comparable_year_ago_period_unavailable). Observed provider quarterly revenue rose sequentially across five quarters: $46.7B, $57.0B, $68.1B, $81.6B, $96.2B; diluted EPS went from $1.08 to $2.46. The Q3 FY27 8-K (filed after the statements in the pipeline snapshot, which end at FQ 2026-07-31, about 110 days old) reports revenue of $115.8B (+103% YoY, +20% QoQ), Data Center revenue of $107.6B (+110% YoY), GAAP diluted EPS of $2.70 and non-GAAP EPS of $2.68. It guides Q4 FY27 revenue to $130.0B plus or minus 3%. The ~$2.48 consensus estimate cited in news was NOT verified. Inference: top-line momentum continues, with sequential growth of roughly 12%-20% per quarter.
key_risks: Gross-margin compression: the Q4 FY27 outlook guides GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin to 71.0%-72.0%, versus 74.8%/74.9% in Q3 FY27 (8-K, SEC).

Debt and cash-conversion volatility: provider total debt jumped from $12.35B to $38.35B, and FCF fell from $48.6B to $21.4B in the quarter ended 2026-07-31. FCF recovered to $43.8B in Q3 FY27 per the 8-K.

Export controls and China: per management's statement (10-Q filed 2026-08-26, Risk Factors), export controls have disrupted and may disrupt the supply chain and distribution and hurt demand even outside China. The 10-K filed 2026-02-25 (Business) says the Chinese government has discouraged purchases of NVIDIA data center products.

Supply/demand mismatch and supplier dependence: per the 10-K filed 2026-02-25 (Risk Factors summary), long manufacturing lead times and third-party supplier dependency could cause supply-demand mismatches. Per the 10-K (Business), the supply chain is concentrated in Asia.

Analyst sentiment softening: the current-month count of hold ratings rose to 14 (from 2 a month earlier) and buy ratings fell to 36 (from 49). Price is 36% below the 52-week high, and the fundamental data does not explain this drawdown.
key_strengths: Q3 FY27 revenue of $115.8B (+103% YoY), with Data Center revenue of $107.6B (+110% YoY), per the 8-K (SEC).
Q4 FY27 revenue guidance of $130.0B plus or minus 3% implies continued sequential growth (inference from the guide midpoint).
Very high profitability: gross margin of ~75% across the last three provider quarters and 74.8% GAAP in Q3 FY27; operating margin of 66.2% in the quarter ended 2026-07-31.

Strong cash generation and capital return: Q3 FY27 operating cash flow of $48.3B and FCF of $43.8B; $28.1B returned to shareholders in Q3; a $150B buyback addition leaves ~$227.3B authorization remaining (8-K).
Liquid balance sheet: Q3 FY27 cash plus marketable debt securities of ~$53.5B, plus $44.2B of marketable equity securities, against ~$32.4B of long-term debt (8-K; the summation is inference).
fundamentals.summary: The Q3 FY27 8-K shows revenue of $115.8B (+103% YoY), 74.8% GAAP gross margin, $43.8B FCF, and a $130B Q4 guide, extending a five-quarter sequential growth run; provider-reported trailing P/E is ~19.7 after a 36% drawdown. Offsets are the guided gross-margin step-down to 71%-72%, the jump in debt in the July quarter, rising analyst hold counts, and export-control risk. The pipeline lacks same-basis P/E and comparable YoY growth, so the view is buy at medium confidence rather than high.

sentiment.news_summary: Observed events (2026-11-09 to 2026-11-17): the board opened an independent probe into Jensen Huang's affair with a woman US intelligence reportedly believes passed information to Beijing; shares fell ~4.3% on 11-09 and ~5.5% on 11-10 (CNBC), a proposed shareholder class action was filed in San Jose, and Trump said the FBI is investigating. Huang resigned as CEO and director effective immediately (8-K, 2026-11-12; SF Standard, DCD); CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey Jones board chair. Pre-earnings, UBS cut its target $300->$240, Bernstein downgraded to a neutral-equivalent with a $200 target, Seaport kept Sell with a $130 target, while BofA held Buy/$280 (as reported by TipRanks). Shares fell in 12 of the 15 sessions before the print (Reuters via MarketScreener) and traded near $152 (TradingNews). On 2026-11-17 after the close, Q3 FY27 revenue was $115.8B (+103% y/y) vs ~$109B expected and EPS $2.68 vs $2.48; Q4 guide was $130B +/-3% vs ~$125B consensus. Nvidia said it will not reinstate Huang, and Kress said the roadmap is on track (CNN, CBS, TechCrunch). Shares rose ~1-4% after hours to ~$161.6. The $150B buyback increase was reported as a September action, not new with this print. Trefis/Fortune (2026-11-12) tied added pressure to Anthropic's IPO and Nvidia's ~$10B private-placement commitment. No dated post-earnings analyst rating or target changes and no institutional-flow data could be verified.

sentiment.summary: News flow is mixed. A severe governance shock (CEO resignation, spy-linked probe, FBI inquiry, class action) and pre-earnings analyst downgrades drove a sharp selloff. A clear beat-and-raise on 2026-11-17 shows demand did not leave with Huang. Deeply negative positioning into a strong print is a contrarian positive, but the governance overhang, an unresolved CEO search and no verified post-earnings upgrades justify a neutral signal with medium confidence rather than a bullish call.

macro.fed_impact: The Fed is tightening. FRED DFF shows an effective fed funds rate of 3.88% as of 2026-11-16, and CPIAUCSL inflation was 3.72% YoY for 2026-09 (Oct-2025 CPI was never published). The FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and held on 2026-10-28 by a 10-2 vote, with the dissents favouring a hike. Fed funds futures implied about 85% odds of a December hike as of 2026-10-28; the next decision is due 2026-12-09. A higher-for-longer and rising discount rate weighs on long-duration, high-multiple growth equities such as NVDA. NVDA's net-cash balance sheet limits any direct borrowing-cost effect.
macro.interest_rate_outlook: US policy is biased toward a further 25bp hike at the 2026-12-08/09 FOMC. The November jobs report (due 2026-12-04) is the key input, and November CPI (2026-12-10) lands after the decision. BNM held the OPR at 2.75% on 2026-11-05, its eighth straight hold since the July 2025 cut. Analysts expect a 25bp hike to 3.00% in Q1 2027, and the next MPC meeting is on 2027-01-21. Both central banks lean hawkish. The USD-MYR policy gap is about 100-125bp and is stable to narrowing only if BNM hikes first.
macro.fx_impact: Web-sourced, because the snapshot's usd_myr is null. USD/MYR opened at about 4.07 on 2026-11-12, with a 4.07-4.08 range expected on 2026-11-13. It was near 4.06 on 2026-11-04 and about 4.04-4.05 on 2026-11-06, so the ringgit has eased slightly against the dollar in November. Commerzbank (2026-11-07) sees near-term consolidation at 4.00-4.10. For a MYR-based holder of USD-denominated NVDA, a stable-to-slightly-firmer USD is mildly supportive in MYR terms near term. An expected BNM hike in Q1 2027 is a modest MYR-appreciation risk that would erode USD returns when translated back to MYR.
sector_macro_factors: CPI year-over-year is for 2026-09 (FRED:CPIAUCSL); inflation of 3.72% is well above the Fed's 2% target, which supports further tightening.
Semiconductor de-rating: the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell about 9-12% on 2026-11-05 (sources differ), its second-worst day on record, on doubts about returns on AI spending after the US midterms.
Yahoo Finance estimated that chip and memory stocks lost about $3.7T in market value between 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-03, amid AI-capex and neocloud-debt concerns.
Hyperscaler capex guidance is reportedly intact (Alphabet about $200B, Amazon about $220B), so the macro risk is valuation and discount rate rather than an observed demand collapse.
macro.summary: The macro backdrop is a headwind for NVDA. The Fed is in a renewed hiking cycle (3.75-4.00% after the 2026-09-16 hike, about 85% December-hike odds as of 2026-10-28) with CPI at 3.72% YoY, and semis suffered a sharp AI-capex-driven de-rating in early November 2026. FX is roughly neutral for the MYR-based holder, with USD/MYR stable around 4.07 (2026-11-12/13) and BNM at 2.75% eyeing a Q1 2027 hike.
